result:
I wrote the record to `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/reader/h3-ghsa-xv7q-fvmc-jx96.json`. The candidate is usable: I recommend a stack of 4 traps out of the 5 I recorded, all independent of each other.

**Protections**
- **P1:** When the OIDC email fallback links a login to an existing local account, it must only trust an email the provider marks as verified (`email_verified`). That flag must come from the same source as the email.
- **P2:** The fallback must only link to a local account whose own email has been confirmed.

**Traps**

| ID | Mechanism | Site | Type | Tier (DeepSeek / MiMo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | M4 | `openid.go:373-381`: the fallback never checks `email_verified`; the claims struct (`openid.go:75-83`) doesn't even have the field. This is the advisory route. | neither | easy / easy |
| T2 | M5 | `openid.go:440-442`: when userinfo is fetched, its email can replace the ID-token email, so the verified flag must follow whichever source supplied the email. | mimo | medium / hard |
| T3 | M11 | `openid.go:478`, `:393-409`, `:410-425`: the fix must not break new-user creation, already-linked logins, or providers that omit the claim or send it as the string `"true"`. A strict bool field fails to decode at `:478` and blocks the whole login. | mimo | medium / hard |
| T4 | M10 | `openid.go:381-390` and `:199-206`: the fallback will link to a local account that is still waiting for email confirmation (`user.go:324-330`). Password login refuses that state (`user.go:371`); the OIDC callback has no equivalent check. | deepseek | xhard / hard |
| T5 | M1 | `openid.go:413-415`: the unverified claim email is written onto an already-linked account on every login. | deepseek | xhard / medium |

**History:** the earlier fix (A, TOTP enforcement at `openid.go:212`) leaves the later bug (B) open. B is in older fallback code that A didn't write, so this is H3b. A's TOTP check only stops the takeover when the victim has TOTP turned on, so B's hidden tests need a victim without TOTP. Nothing was fixed by a dependency upgrade; the fix is in-repo.

**Conflicts and fairness risks**
- Over-hardening for T1 breaks T3: requiring `email_verified` across the whole callback, rather than only in the fallback branch, breaks normal logins.
- The existing test at `openid_test.go:257-275` expects the fallback to link when there is no `email_verified` claim. The task has to update or replace it.
- Some identity providers never send `email_verified`. Admins who deliberately enabled the email fallback for a trusted provider would lose it.
- Deployments without a mailer never confirm local emails, so T4's rule can't be applied there.

**Recommended design: T1, T2, T3, T4.** It includes a deepseek-type trap (T4) and two mimo-type traps (T2, T3). It also uses three different fix sites: the fallback branch, the claims merge, and the decode and creation paths. I left T5 out because I found no route from it to an account takeover.

**Limits**
- I did not inspect B's published fix (`7854f2729ab7`), so I don't know whether it also covers T2–T4.
- T4's real-world impact is uncertain. The attacker can't log into an unconfirmed account they created, and without a mailer that state never occurs.
- Both points are listed under `unverified` in the JSON.

Estimated effort for all independent traps: about 45 minutes.
